title: ALMA and the soft-hued sky
caption: The ALMA array under a soft-hued sky, Chajnantor Plateau
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: This photograph by D. Kordan shows the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, known as ALMA, under a sky that the picture's title calls soft-hued.

For studying the cold Universe, ALMA ranks among the most powerful telescopes in the world. Rather than a single mirror it is an array of antennas, which work together to detect millimeter and submillimeter light. That kind of light comes from cold material such as gas and dust, which gives off little visible light.

The array stands on the Chajnantor Plateau in the Atacama Desert in Chile. Water vapor in the air absorbs the kind of light ALMA studies, so a dry, high site suits it well. The photograph pairs the telescope with the colors of the sky above its desert home.

understand.summary: A ground-based landscape photograph by D. Kordan for ESO, taken in visible light. The colors are those the camera recorded.
understand.eye: The camera records visible light much as the eye does, while ALMA itself observes millimeter and submillimeter light that no eye can see.
